paragraphs: Stephen's death set off a wave of brutal persecution against the church in Jerusalem. The believers scattered all through Judea and Samaria — all except the apostles. Good and brave men buried Stephen, giving him a solemn funeral. There weren't many dry eyes that day.

And Saul went wild, tearing the church apart — barging house after house after house, dragging men and women off to jail. Forced out of their home base, the followers of Jesus became missionaries everywhere. Wherever they were scattered, they preached the Message about Jesus. Philip went down to a Samaritan city and proclaimed the Message of the Messiah. When the people heard what he said and saw the miracles — clear signs of God at work — they hung on his every word. Many who could neither stand nor walk were healed that day. Evil spirits screamed in protest as they were driven out. And the whole city was filled with joy!

Before Philip arrived, a man named Simon had been practicing magic in the city, acting like some famous VIP and dazzling all the Samaritans with his tricks. He had everyone, from little kids to old men, eating out of his hand. They all thought he had supernatural powers and called him 'the Great Wizard.' He'd been around a long time, and pretty much everyone was in awe of him.

But when Philip showed up announcing the news of God's kingdom and proclaiming the name of Jesus Christ, they forgot all about Simon. People were getting baptized left and right, becoming believers in droves! Even Simon himself believed and was baptized. From that moment on, he stuck to Philip like glue — so fascinated by all the God-signs and miracles that he wouldn't leave Philip's side.

When the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had accepted God's Message, they sent Peter and John down to pray for them to receive the Holy Spirit. Up to that point, the new believers had only been baptized in the name of the Master Jesus — the Holy Spirit hadn't fallen on them yet. Then the apostles laid their hands on them, and they did receive the Holy Spirit.

When Simon saw that the apostles could give people the Spirit just by laying hands on them, he pulled out his money, all excited, and said, "Sell me your secret! Show me how you did that! How much do you want? Name your price!"

Peter said, "To heck with you and your money! Do you really think you can buy God's gift? That's unthinkable. You will never be part of what God is doing by making deals and offering bribes. Change your ways — right now! Ask the Master to forgive you for trying to use God to make money. I can tell this is an old habit of yours — you reek of money-lust."
"Oh!" said Simon. "Please pray for me! Pray to the Master that nothing like that will ever happen to me!"
And with that, the apostles headed out — still witnessing and spreading the Message of God's salvation, preaching in every Samaritan town they passed on their way back to Jerusalem.

Later, God's angel spoke to Philip: "At noon today, I want you to walk over to that deserted road that goes from Jerusalem down to Gaza." He got up and went. On the road he met an Ethiopian eunuch traveling back home. The eunuch had been on a pilgrimage to Jerusalem and was returning to Ethiopia, where he served as the minister in charge of all the finances of Candace, the queen of the Ethiopians. He was riding in a chariot, reading the prophet Isaiah.
The Spirit told Philip, "Go catch up with that chariot." Philip ran alongside, and when he heard the eunuch reading Isaiah, he asked, "Do you understand what you're reading?"

He replied, "How could I, with no one to guide me?" and invited Philip to climb up into the chariot beside him. The Scripture passage he was reading went like this: "Like a sheep led off to slaughter, like a lamb silent before its shearers — he never said a word. He was humiliated and denied justice. And who can count his descendants now that he has been taken from the earth?"
The eunuch said, "Tell me — who is the prophet talking about here: himself, or someone else?" Philip jumped at the chance. Starting from that very passage, he told him all about Jesus.

As they continued down the road, they came to a stream of water. The eunuch said, "Look — water! What's stopping me from getting baptized?" He ordered the chariot to stop. They both went down into the water, and Philip baptized him right there. When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of God suddenly whisked Philip away — and that was the last the eunuch ever saw of him. But he didn't mind. He had found what he'd come for, and he went on down the road happier than he'd ever been.
Philip showed up in Azotus and kept heading north, preaching the Message in every village along the route until he arrived at Caesarea.
title: The Magician and the Road Trip
